deep.reconstruction:
Context: this page follows the 'Zur Astralgeometrie' notes on the angle-defect/area theorem. Here Gauss lays a foundation for the plane that does not use the parallel postulate, i.e. within absolute geometry.

(1) Definition. Fix a point A and a line AB. The plane P(A,AB) is the surface made up of all lines AD through A with angle BAD = 90°. Equivalently, it is swept out when AD rotates about the axis AB.

(2) Extend BA beyond A to C. Then CAD is the supplement of BAD, so AC is also perpendicular to every AD.

(3) Lemma: if AD, AD' lie in P with AD = AD', then every point T of the line DD' lies in P.
Take C on the extension of BA with AC = AB.
- The four-point systems ACD'D and ABDD' are congruent, via A→A, C→B, D'→D, D→D'.
- Justification (mine): triangles CAD' and BAD are congruent by SAS (AC = AB, AD' = AD, right angles at A), so CD' = BD. Likewise CD = BD'.
- Hence triangle CD'D is congruent to triangle BDD'.
- Triangles BAD and BAD' are congruent by SAS, so BD = BD'. Hence triangle BD'D is congruent to BDD'.
- Combining: CD'D is congruent to BD'D. So CD = BD, CD' = BD', and angle CDD' = angle BDD'.
- For T on line DD', triangles BDT and CDT are congruent by SAS (BD = CD, DT common, equal angles at D; for T beyond D use the supplementary angles). So BT = CT.
- Triangle BCT is therefore isosceles, so it is congruent to CBT (equal base angles).
- Then triangles BAT and CAT are congruent (BA = CA, BT = CT, equal angles at B and C; or simply SSS).
- So angle BAT = angle CAT. These are supplementary, hence both are right, and T lies in P.
- In modern terms: the chord-line DD' lies in the locus {X : XB = XC}, and points of that locus see AB at a right angle from A.

(4) Theorem: if T and V lie in P, the whole line TV lies in P.
- Case I: A is on TV. Then TV is the line AT, which is perpendicular to AB, so it lies in P by definition.
- Case II: A is not on TV and AT = AV. This is Lemma 3 with D = T, D' = V.
- Case III: AT > AV.
  - Extend TA beyond A to K with AK = AT.
  - The circle of radius AT about A, swept by T under rotation about AB, passes through K.
  - The disc it bounds lies in P and is cut by the diameter KT into two halves. V (with AV < AT) lies in one of them.
  - Let the chord TW turn about T with W running along the semicircle K…W from K to T. Each chord has AT = AW, so by Lemma 3 its full line lies in P.
  - The moving chord sweeps the half-disc, so in some position it passes through the given interior point.
  - The proof finishes on the next page: the given line is part of a chord-line, which lies wholly in P. The next page also adds a rigorous sphere/continuity argument that the half-disc is really exhausted.
- Note on naming: the figure and the next page label the interior point U and the arc point V. Gauss evidently switched names after the crossed-out line 'es geschehe in V'.

Purpose: to derive the incidence property of planes (Euclid's line-in-plane axiom) from a definition by perpendiculars, using only congruence and no parallels. He needs this as groundwork for the non-Euclidean area theory on the previous page.
errors: Labeling inconsistency: the theorem is stated for points T, V and the text places V inside the half-disc. The figure and the continuation instead have U as the interior point and V on the periphery (the crossed-out line 'es geschehe in V' shows the change). This is a naming slip, not a logical error.

Step 3 states 'ABDD' deckt ACD'D' without justification. It follows from SAS twice (AC = AB, AD = AD', right angles at A) but is left implicit. The step from 'BCT and CBT coincide' to 'BAT and CAT coincide' is likewise implicit (SAS or SSS).
In step 3, 'T beliebig in der geraden DD'' covers the whole line. For T outside the segment, the angle equality at D must be taken as the supplement; this is correct but unremarked.
Case III relies on the moving chord sweeping the whole half-disc, a continuity argument. On this page it is only asserted; Gauss supplies a proof on the next page.

Implicit assumptions: the set swept by AD is a surface/disc in which a diameter separates two halves, and the degenerate case where D, A, D' are collinear is ignored. That case is covered by Case I/definition.

results.what: Definition of the plane as the union of all perpendiculars to a line AB at a point A (the surface swept by a rotating perpendicular)
results.modern_name: Plane as locus of perpendiculars (cf. Euclid XI.5); foundations of absolute geometry
results.usually_credited_to: Euclid (XI.5, as a theorem); proposed as a definition by various 18th-19th c. authors (e.g. Crelle 1834 discussed several definitions)

results.what: Lemma: if AD = AD' are perpendiculars to AB at A, every point of line DD' is equidistant from B and C (AB = AC) and hence lies in the plane
results.modern_name: Identification of the perpendicular-plane with the perpendicular-bisector locus {X: XB = XC}; neutral-geometry congruence argument
results.usually_credited_to: Equidistance definition of the plane: Leibniz; Fourier (1795); used by J. Bolyai and Lobachevsky (1830s)

results.what: Theorem: the line through two points of the plane lies wholly in it, proved without the parallel postulate by a rotating-chord sweep
results.modern_name: Line–plane incidence axiom derived from a congruence-based definition of the plane (absolute geometry)
results.usually_credited_to: Treated in Bolyai/Lobachevsky foundations and Crelle's 'Zur Theorie der Ebene' (1834); Gauss's non-Euclidean notes partly published by Stäckel in Werke VIII

deep.surprise_reason: Gauss's interest in founding the plane independently of the parallel postulate is known from the Astralgeometrie notes in Werke VIII and his reactions to Crelle and Bolyai. The arguments are elementary congruence proofs. It is a nice unpublished-looking detail, but not a new result.

checkable.sympy: b,r,t,s=symbols('b r t s',real=True); A=Matrix([0,0,0]); B=Matrix([0,0,b]); C=Matrix([0,0,-b]); D=Matrix([r,0,0]); Dp=Matrix([r*cos(t),r*sin(t),0]); T=D+s*(Dp-D); simplify((T-B).dot(T-B)-(T-C).dot(T-C))==0
checkable.asserts: Lemma 3 (Euclidean model): every point T of line DD' (AD = AD' perpendicular to AB) is equidistant from B and C.
Conclusion of Lemma 3: angle BAT is right, i.e. T lies in the plane of perpendiculars at A.
Intermediate congruence CD = BD and CD' = BD' (CD'D congruent to BD'D).
In the Euclidean model the equidistance locus {XB = XC} is exactly the plane z = 0 perpendicular to AB at A, matching the perpendicular definition.

transcription_corrections: The left-margin fragments (Flächen, Inhalt = Δ, (… i.24)^2 = 1, Summe … Flächenin-, beruhet, beides durch Constr., Cf. S. 268, (A+B+C)) are bleed-through/facing page from the previous Astralgeometrie page, not part of folio 153.
Figure at bottom left: labels are K (top), A, T (bottom), V on the arc, U inside the half-disc, W on the lower arc. The interior point is therefore U, consistent with the next page's 'TU'.
Last line reads approximately 'beschreibt sie das Planum, [-und indem-] vollendet die Figur immer vollkommner und hat'. 'Figur' is a plausible reading of the abbreviated word.
'{+linie+}' is written above 'Kreis', giving 'Kreislinie welche T durch Drehung um A beschreibt'; this is correctly captured.
Small mark to the left of 'Ebne' in heading area ('Idw'/'Ibr'?) is a later archival/pencil annotation, not Gauss's text.
